rules.label: fiscale
rules.notes: Retention period for the documents/records on which the tax authority may exercise its audit and reassessment rights — 6 years. Carried over from the pre-refactor git tag (compliance/profiles/fr.ts), where this duration had been conflated with the 10-year commercial one (see documentation/internal/audit/03-LEGAL-VERIFICATION.md, entry FR-D9, and documentation/internal/DECISIONS.md, D-001) — this file fixes the confusion by declaring BOTH, never by picking just one. Origin (2026-09-13, revision of the origin axis): article L102 B itself could not be retrieved as raw text (legifrance.gouv.fr returns 403/Cloudflare from this environment, including via web.archive.org, whose snapshot contains only the empty JS shell); the official administrative doctrine BOI-CF-COM-10-10-30 (version in force as of 03/09/2025, bofip.impots.gouv.fr), which quotes and comments on this same article, states verbatim: « Le délai de six ans court à compter de la date de la dernière opération mentionnée sur les livres ou registres ou de la date à laquelle les documents ou pièces ont été établis. » — i.e. the document's own ESTABLISHMENT date (issuance), day for day, never a calendar year-end nor the moment of archiving. The same BOI doctrine adds: « Le délai de six ans s'applique également aux factures sous format papier ou électronique qui tiennent lieu de pièces justificatives... » — so it does cover the invoice.

rules.label: commerciale
rules.notes: Retention period for accounting records (books, registers) and supporting documents — 10 years. This is the duration the pre-refactor tag's FR profile already applied (10 years), but under the mistaken name "fiscale" — see FR-D9: "the tax duration is 6 years (LPF L102 B); the 10 years fall under commercial law (C. com. L123-22)." Origin (2026-09-13): the current text of L123-22, retrieved via web.archive.org (2019-09-09 snapshot of legifrance.gouv.fr's old HTML template, the only one reachable from this environment — the modern template is blocked by Cloudflare), states only « Les documents comptables et les pièces justificatives sont conservés pendant dix ans. » — WITHOUT itself specifying a starting point. The implementing decree (C. com. art. R123-177, LEGIARTI000030927443) is the one generally understood to run this period from the financial year's closing, but its text could not be retrieved (no archive.org snapshot under either the old or new template; the new template returns the Incapsula challenge page even in the archived snapshot). For lack of a literal confirmation of R123-177 AND for lack of a product field carrying a company's own financial-year-end date (nothing on `Company` stores it), this file applies the SAFE reading this module imposes as a matter of principle (never shorten): origin `fiscalYearEndUnknownSafe`, i.e. issue date + one full calendar year — always ≥ the true financial-year close regardless of its alignment (see compute-retention.ts). Data that would make this point exact: the raw text of R123-177, and/or each company's own real financial-year-end date.

notes: The two obligations above bind the same company SIMULTANEOUSLY — they are not two competing estimates of the same duration, nor a choice to make. An invoice a company could no longer produce after 6 years would put it in breach of the commercial obligation (10 years) if it had destroyed it; the EFFECTIVE retention floor is therefore their MAXIMUM — see compute-retention.ts. This is not settling FR-D9 by inventing a duration: it is applying both cited texts at once, exactly what D-001 (documentation/internal/DECISIONS.md) called for: "the product should probably carry both rather than choosing one." Sources: carried over from the pre-refactor git tag; LPF art. L102 B (via BOI-CF-COM-10-10-30, bofip.impots.gouv.fr, version in force as of 03/09/2025) and C. com. art. L123-22 (via web.archive.org, 2019-09-09 snapshot of legifrance.gouv.fr); re-checked directly again on 2026-09-13 for the origin axis (each rule now carries its own starting point — see the per-rule notes above for the detail and the limits of what could be verified as raw text in that session).
